subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: The pledges at Aqabah, the Hijrah and zakah
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y5 lesson 18 (Mushaf or printed at-Tawbah 9:60 (translation of the meaning))
intro: Lesson 18: Who receives zakah? Sadaqah and zakah compared. To understand who Allah says may receive zakah and how zakah differs from sadaqah

questions.q: Explain two differences between zakah and sadaqah.
questions.a: Zakah is compulsory at 2.5% on savings above nisab for the eight groups; sadaqah is voluntary, any amount, to anyone.
questions.model: Point: zakah is a duty, sadaqah is a choice. Evidence: zakah is a pillar; sadaqah is any good deed. Explain: zakah has a set amount and set recipients (9:60). Link: both please Allah.

questions.q: Name three of the eight groups.
questions.a: For example: the poor, the needy, the traveller

questions.q: Zakah quiz and case cards on the pupil PDF: decide whether each person may receive zakah (example cases), then write a sadaqah plan for your week.
questions.a: Correct decisions using 9:60; a realistic sadaqah plan
questions.model: Teacher does case 1: 'A family who cannot pay for food: yes, they are among the poor and needy.'

questions.q: why does Allah list the recipients Himself?
questions.a: So zakah reaches the right people fairly.

questions.q: name one good cause that could be 'in the way of Allah'.
questions.a: For example: spreading knowledge of Islam (scholars differ on what is included)

questions.q: Back to our ponder: who should get it first?
questions.a: Those Allah names in 9:60, such as the poor and needy.
